column1: # THE FLEET. One row per class. Tab separated, so a blurb can hold commas and apostrophes freely.
# Edit here (or in a spreadsheet, exported as TSV), then: npm run import && npm run catalogue
# Lines starting with # are ignored, so notes and section breaks are fine.
# id          a short camelCase name, unique. Becomes the key everything else refers to.
# name        what a captain reads. Sentence case, no em dashes, no interpuncts.
# price       coins to buy the bare hull. 0 for the ship she starts with.
# hull, crew  maximum health in the same points the bars already use.
# speed       her own pace before a stitch of canvas. About 1. Fine lines are higher.
# hand        how she answers her rudder, before canvas. About 1. Small ships are higher.
# canvas      how much sail she WANTS to get moving. The most important number here: it is why a
#             half-rigged big ship is genuinely bad, and why the same suit drives a cutter hard.
# tons        what she carries before her guns start telling on her handling.
# broadside   guns A SIDE, mirrored. bow and swivel are totals.
# masts       where she can step one, "station/size", space separated, bow aft.
#             stations: fore main mizzen      sizes: small medium large
# bowsprit    yes or no.
# blurb       one line a captain reads on the card.
# LEAVE speed, hand, canvas OR tons BLANK if you would rather not place them by hand. Say so and
# they can be derived from her size and rig, then tuned against `npm run catalogue`.

column15: One mast, a handful of guns, and nothing spare. She turns inside anything afloat.

column1: sloop
column15: Still one mast, but a tall one, and enough deck to work four guns a side.

column1: brig
column15: Two masts and a real broadside. The first hull that can take a beating and answer it.

column1: frigate
column15: Three masts, eight guns a side, and the speed to choose her fights.

column1: galleon
column15: Ten guns a side and a crew to work them. Slow to start, and slow to stop.
